text:
ben: Heads up — we're seeing a cluster of GPU attach holds in eu-west1 after last night's thermal rotation window. Lots of Preemptible nodes stuck in Pending for >3m. I traced to localcache index lock storms and metadata queue depth spikes on the local NVMe (nvme0).

nisha: ugh. are these the nodes that had the fan PWM bump?

ben: yes, same cohort. pattern: after rotation we had a large background revalidate + aggressive batch backfill. attach attempts pile up, then kworker spikes, then attach times blow out.

sam: can you paste the dmesg / kernel stack where lock contention shows up?

ben: ```
[ 1234.567890] overlayfs: revalidate: index_lock contended (owner=kworker/0:5)
[ 1234.568123] nvme0: metadata_qdepth=256 -> qdep hit 240+
[ 1234.568456] attach: pod/worker-abc waiting for device attach (timeout 30s)
```

maria: sounds like localcache GC + revalidate are colliding with many small writes from the backfill. That cohort's write pattern is tiny-random which amplifies queue depth on those drives.

ben: agreed. I spun up a probe disabling the background revalidate on 5 nodes and attach latency dropped from ~45s to ~6s for new pods.

infra-bot: alert: gpu-provisioning-delay eu-west1 duration=7m affected=18

nisha: two possible mitigations: 1) temporarily throttle the backfill job concurrency (n=2 per host) 2) reduce localcache spill/eviction pressure (raise KVCACHE_SPILL_THRESHOLD or lower concurrent GC workers).

ben: tried lowering parallelism of backfill -> immediate improvement. I'm going to flip KVCACHE_SPILL_THRESHOLD to 0.7 on the cohort to reduce NVMe write fanout and see.

sam: also consider preventing overlayfs revalidate during high attach windows (we can gate it behind a rolling maintenance flag).

ops-watch: rolling change propagated to 5/5 canaries: `export KVCACHE_SPILL_THRESHOLD=0.7 && systemctl restart localcache-gc`

ben: canary looks good. attach tail latencies: before 45s, after 6s. NVMe qdepth now stays under 120.

maria: ok please do a gradual rollout and open a follow-up to tune default thresholds. We should also add a probe to detect simultaneous high revalidate + backfill and auto-throttle.

ben: noted — will open RFC + runbook. For immediate: continuing rollout across eu-west1 and throttling backfills for 30m.

nisha: thanks, and let's add the cohort ID to the incident so we can correlate wear metrics later (I suspect these nodes have tighter thermal headroom so the write bursts hit controller slow paths). :eyes:

ben: done — added cohort tag and created ticket #INFRA-4318 for postmortem and threshold tuning.

maria: great work catching root cause quickly. :thumbsup:
